name: bluewater-27-heinz
lines: In eighteen sixty nine, a lot of bottled food came in dark glass. For a reason.
You could not see what was inside. And what was inside was often not what you paid for.
One young man put his in clear glass. So you could see every bit of it.
That one choice grew into one of the biggest food companies on earth.
His name was Henry Heinz. Here is his story. And four moves you can take from it.
Pennsylvania. A small town near Pittsburgh. Henry is in his twenties.
He sells grated horseradish. From his mother's recipe.
So does everybody else. And the trade has a dirty secret.
Sellers stretch it. With turnip. With wood fibre. With leaves.
And they bottle it in coloured glass. So you cannot tell.
Henry does the opposite. Pure horseradish. In a clear bottle.
His whole pitch is one look. Hold it up to the light.
Shops take it. Customers trust it. Sales climb.
Move one. If your work is good, let them see all of it.
Then it goes wrong. In eighteen seventy five, after a crash in the economy, his company goes bankrupt.
He is thirty one. And he has lost it all.
Two months later he starts again. With his brother and his cousin.
Same idea. Clean food. Nothing hidden.
And he adds a second idea. Do not tell people it is good. Let them taste it.
At fairs. In grocery stores. His people hand out samples. And explain how the food is made.
Move two. A taste beats a claim.
Chicago. Eighteen ninety three. The World's Fair. Millions of visitors.
Heinz has a big stand. In a terrible spot. Upstairs. Far from the crowd.
Nobody climbs the stairs.
He does not complain to the fair.
He offers a free gift to anyone who comes up.
A tiny green pickle. To pin on your coat.
Hundreds of thousands of people climb those stairs.
They taste the food. They take the pickle. And they wear it home.
Every one of them is now a walking advertisement.
Move three. Bad location? Give them a reason to come to you.
Three years later, he wants a slogan.
He picks a number. Fifty seven varieties.
Here is the funny part. He already sells more than sixty.
He just likes the number. So fifty seven it is.
He puts it everywhere. And lights it up in New York, on what was called the biggest electric sign in the world.
A number is easier to remember than a promise.
Move four. Give people one thing to remember.
From one clear bottle of horseradish, to a name known around the world.
So here are the four. One. Show the whole job. Photos. Video. Nothing hidden.
Two. Let them try you before they have to trust you.
Three. If they will not come to you, give them a reason.
And four. Pick one thing to be known for. And say it everywhere.
He did not win by shouting louder. He won by having nothing to hide.
Your business. Our marketing department. Bluewater Co.
